prediction.likelyOutcome: Waterwood is very likely to establish liability for breach of the repair and surrender covenant given the City's own pre-suit and trial admissions on the roof and asphalt, but is unlikely to recover full replacement-cost damages across the roof, HVAC, and paving given the lease's express wear-and-tear exclusion and the sharply contested replace-vs-repair scope. A split verdict in the roughly $75,000-$110,000 range (before any fee award) is more probable than recovery at or near the $150,000 alleged ceiling, with the parties' CCP 998 offers ($40,001 City / $120,000 Waterwood) creating real post-verdict cost-shifting stakes in either direction.

outcome.description: After a 10-day jury trial the jury found the City breached the lease and awarded Waterwood a lump sum of $45,050 in contract damages (plus $1,987.06 interest; Waterwood was awarded $19,905.04 in costs). The trial court then found the City the prevailing party for contractual fees and ordered Waterwood to pay the City $172,375 in attorney fees. On December 18, 2020 the Second District affirmed in part and reversed the fee award to the City, remanding with the trial court limited to finding Waterwood the prevailing party or no prevailing party. The damages award was not disturbed.
